ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26
(1) Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Article 5
Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, termination/loss of pregnancy, loss of consciousness and/or causes the death of women and/or children.

SANCTIONS
Article 32

Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 33. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 34. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 35. Protection of women is all efforts made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 36. Implementation of Child Protection is a series of activities carried out by the Regional Government, community, and parents, aimed at preventing, reducing risks, and handling victims of acts of violence, exploitation, abuse and neglect of children. 37. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, be healthy, intelligent, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination. 38. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, social including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 39. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and psychologically. 40. Violence Against Women and Children in the Household is any act against a woman and child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere. 41. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that can harm welfare and growth and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if there is restriction or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights. 42. Child Abuse is any action against a child, including placing a child in a situation that can cause adverse impacts on the welfare, safety, dignity and development of the child. 43. Assistance is social work that has professional competence in its field. 44. Child Neglect is any act of neglecting the fulfillment of basic needs, care, and maintenance that interferes with or hinders child development, including leaving a child in a dangerous situation. 45. Prevention is the effort of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect of children. 46. Risk Reduction is early action toward children and their families who are in vulnerable situations or at risk of experiencing various forms of violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect. 47. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of children who become victims of acts of violence, abuse, exploitation, and or neglect. 48. Care Environment is care by parents and care outside parental care. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 53. Repatriation is an Effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or receiving area to the area of origin. 55. Social reintegration is an Effort to reunite witnesses and/or victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for witnesses and/or victims. 56. Child participation is the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly carried out with the consent and will of the child based on awareness and understanding. 60.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs and the interests of the local community on its own initiative based on community aspirations within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 2. Regional Government is the administration of government affairs by the regional government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration of Tanggamus Regency. 4. Regent is the Regent of Tanggamus. 5. Regional Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Tanggamus Regency. 6. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA DALDUK and KB is the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tanggamus Regency. 9. Sub-district is the working area of the sub-district head as a regional apparatus of Tanggamus regency. 10. Village or called Pekon, hereinafter referred to as village/pekon, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage the interests of the local community, based on origins and customs that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 11. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb. 12. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the State. 13. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a parent or body that in fact exercises custody power as a parent over a child. 16. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. 17. Child Marriage is a marriage conducted through civil, religious or customary law with or without registration or official consent where one or both partners are children under the age of 18 years. 18. Children in Need of Special Protection hereinafter abbreviated as AMPK are Children in need of special protection. 19. Worst Forms of Child Labor hereinafter referred to as BPTA is the worst forms of child labor. 20. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 21. Street child is a child whose life is irregular, spending most of their time outside the home to earn a living on the streets or in public places. 22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their growth and development normally. 23. Gifted child is a child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 24. Child in conflict with the law is a child who conflicts with the law, a child who becomes a victim of a criminal act, and a child who becomes a witness to a criminal act. 25. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education and raising of that Child into the environment of the Family of adoptive Parents based on a court decision or determination. 26. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the normal growth and development of the Child. 27. Economically exploited child is an action with or without the consent of the child who becomes a victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical exploitation, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a child by another party to obtain material benefits. 28. Sexually exploited child is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of a child to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and sexual abuse. 29. Child labor is children both male and female who are involved in economic activities that interfere with or hinder the growth and development process and are dangerous to the physical and mental health of children. 30. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect and develop Children in accordance with their religion and in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests. 31. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government and regional government. 32.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 28
(1) The regional government carries out Guidance and Supervision by means of:
a. Coordination
b. Guidance
c. Education and Training
d. Monitoring and Evaluation
(2) The implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out among stakeholders cross-sectorally with Regional Apparatus and community organizations/institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) The implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b for women and children who become victims is carried out through guidance on religious values and social values, counseling, social rehabilitation, and social assistance by the competent Regional Apparatus together with other related agencies.
(4) The implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is provided to women and children who become victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the competent Regional Apparatus, Work Training Centers, and other related agencies.
(5) The implementation of guidance and supervision for women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3), and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

Considering : a. that in order to protect the constitutional rights of women and children in accordance with the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the Regional Government is obligated to be responsible in organizing the protection of women and children against acts of violence; b. that to fulfill the indicators of the Implementation of Child-Friendly Regency, concerning protection services, prevention of violence against women and children, regulations are needed to govern the various roles of regional apparatus institutions and other institutions; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Organization of Protection of Women and Children; In View of : 1. OF

NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

(1) Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26
(1) Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 13 letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as members of the family.

CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Article 28

a. Coordination
b. Guidance
c. Education and Training
d. Monitoring and Evaluation
(2) The implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out among stakeholders cross-sectorally with Regional Apparatus and community organizations/institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) The implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b for women and children who become victims is carried out through guidance on religious values and social values, counseling, social rehabilitation, and social assistance by the competent Regional Apparatus together with other related agencies.
(4) The implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is provided to women and children who become victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the competent Regional Apparatus, Work Training Centers, and other related agencies.
(5) The implementation of guidance and supervision for women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3), and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

OF

NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

OF

NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26
(1) Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

Article 26
(1) Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

OF

NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

Considering : a. that in order to protect the constitutional rights of women and children in accordance with the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the Regional Government is obligated to be responsible in organizing the protection of women and children against acts of violence; b. that to fulfill the indicators of the Implementation of Child-Friendly Regency, concerning protection services, prevention of violence against women and children, regulations are needed to govern the various roles of regional apparatus institutions and other institutions; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Organization of Protection of Women and Children; In View of : 1. ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

 a. Preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;

 c. Participating in the handling of victims of violence.

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER VII
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Part One
Prevention of violence against women and children

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

OF

NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

Considering : a. that in order to protect the constitutional rights of women and children in accordance with the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the Regional Government is obligated to be responsible in organizing the protection of women and children against acts of violence; b. that to fulfill the indicators of the Implementation of Child-Friendly Regency, concerning protection services, prevention of violence against women and children, regulations are needed to govern the various roles of regional apparatus institutions and other institutions; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Organization of Protection of Women and Children; In View of : 1. I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 28
(1) The regional government carries out Guidance and Supervision by means of:
a. Coordination
b. Guidance
c. Education and Training
d. Monitoring and Evaluation
(2) The implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out among stakeholders cross-sectorally with Regional Apparatus and community organizations/institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) The implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b for women and children who become victims is carried out through guidance on religious values and social values, counseling, social rehabilitation, and social assistance by the competent Regional Apparatus together with other related agencies.
(4) The implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is provided to women and children who become victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the competent Regional Apparatus, Work Training Centers, and other related agencies.
(5) The implementation of guidance and supervision for women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3), and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

Article 15
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community as referred to in Article 13 letter b and letter c, shall be implemented in the form of participation of the private sector and the community.
(2) The form of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
 a. Preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
 b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the authorized parties; and
 c. Participating in the handling of victims of violence.
(3) The form of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XI
FUNDING
Article 30
Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and
b. Other legal and non-binding sources.

Article 8
Neglect as referred to in Article 4 letter d includes: a. Acts of deliberately neglecting a woman within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obligated to provide livelihood and care to said woman.
b. Acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs in a proper manner, whether physical, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for his/her care.
c. Acts of deliberately neglecting to care for or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for his/her care.

CHAPTER XII
SANCTIONS
Article 32
In the event of violence against Women and Children, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of the Laws and Regulations.

NUMBER 2 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as the protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic manner and inseparable from one another. Community-based services are the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and child victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26
(1) Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 33. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 34. Implementation of Child Protection is a series of activities carried out by the Regional Government, community, and parents, aimed at preventing, reducing risks, and handling victims of acts of violence, exploitation, abuse and neglect of children. 37.
